If you want to make money online selling digital products, keep it simple: 1️⃣ Pick a problem people already want solved. Don’t create something just because you like it. Find a problem people are already looking for help with. 🎯 2️⃣ Create a simple solution. Turn your knowledge into something useful. A PDF 📄 A guide 📚 A checklist ✅ A template 📝 A mini course 🎓 It doesn’t need to be perfect. It needs to be useful. 3️⃣ Create content around the problem. Teach people for free. 🎥 Give them tips. Show them what they’re doing wrong. Share what you’re learning. Give them small wins. Your content should make people think: “If this is free, imagine what I could learn from the full product.” 👀 4️⃣ Make your offer clear. Tell people: 👉 What it is 👉 Who it’s for 👉 What problem it solves 👉 What they’ll get 👉 Why it can help them Don’t make people guess why they should buy. 5️⃣ Stay consistent. 📈 You don’t need millions of followers to make money online. You need the right people seeing the right content consistently. And stop worrying about people who don’t believe in you. They can laugh. They can doubt you. They can say it won’t work. Let them. 😂 You’re not building your future to impress them. Build. Learn. Post. Improve. Repeat. 🔥 Then let the results speak for themselves. Don't ask ChatGPT, "What digital product should I sell?" Instead, ask: "What problems are people currently paying to solve?" Then, pick one problem you genuinely understand. One of the biggest mistakes new digital sellers make is starting with the product. They ask: "What e-book should I make?" or "What template should I sell?" This is backwards. Start with the problem. People don't buy a PDF because they desperately want another file on their phone. They buy because they want to: 1. Save money 2. Save time 3. Learn something faster 4. Get organized 5. Avoid mistakes 6. Reach a specific goal So, open ChatGPT and ask: "What problems are people currently paying to solve? Give me 20 problems that could be turned into simple digital products. For each one, tell me who has the problem, what result they want, and what type of digital product could help?" Don't create anything yet! Just look at the 20 problems first.
